 8 highly anticipated K-Dramas releasing this November you can't miss 
 Dive into November's diverse K-Drama releases, blending romance, history and suspense... November's upcoming slate of K-dramas brings a captivating mix of storytelling Srushti Kulkarni Updated on :  02 Nov 2026, 4:47 am 
 Copied 
 November's upcoming slate of Korean dramas brings a captivating mix of storytelling designed to pull viewers into starkly different worlds. From lavish royal court intrigues and sprawling historical war sagas to gritty cross-border crime investigations and dark academic thrillers, the month spans a wide spectrum of dramatic depth. Alongside these intense narratives, lighthearted office romances, high-octane legal rematches, and comedic crime-solving units balance out the lineup — offering an impressive variety for every type of viewer looking to update their watchlist.
 What to watch this November: The ultimate guide to new K-drama releases
 1. The Remarried Empress
 A highly anticipated webtoon adaptation weaves a grand tale of royal ambition Opening the month's premier releases on November 4 via Disney+ and Hulu, this highly anticipated webtoon adaptation weaves a grand tale of royal ambition, heartbreak and calculated revenge. Shin Min-a stars as Empress Navier, a deeply intelligent and dutiful monarch whose world shatters when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu, takes a former slave as his mistress and breaks his vow of fidelity. 
 2. Good Partner (Season 2)
 The second season of the hit legal series shifts its lens to the grueling realities of boutique practice Returning to SBS on November 20, the second season of the hit legal series shifts its lens from corporate firm politics to the grueling realities of boutique practice. The new chapter introduces fresh workplace friction as Kim Hye-yoon joins the cast as a fiercely empathetic junior lawyer whose heart-on-her-sleeve approach directly clashes with Eun-kyung's pragmatic, emotionally detached strategy. Supported by returning cast members P.O and Ji Seung-hyun alongside newcomer Park Hae-jin, the 16-episode series explores high-stakes matrimonial court battles alongside the personal growth required to rebuild from the ground up.
 3. Sword & Silence
 The 28-episode epic chronicles intense military campaigns Debuting on KBS2 on November 14, this 30-billion-won production brings a sweeping, authentic historical sageuk to weekend primetime. Set during the turbulent era of the Three Kingdoms, the 28-episode epic chronicles the intense military campaigns and diplomatic maneuverings that shaped the unification of the Korean peninsula. Lee Hyun-wook leads the narrative alongside Jang Hyuk as the formidable Goguryeo dictator Yeon Gaesomun, Park Sung-woong as General Kim Yu-sin, and Kim Kang-woo as King Taejong Muyeol
 4. Nine to Six
 The series delves into the friction between professional ambitions and genuine emotional connection Premiering November 25 on SBS, this office romantic comedy takes a lighthearted look at corporate survival and rigid workplace boundaries. Directed by Lee Hyung-min, the story centers on Kang Ji-yi, portrayed by Park Min-young, a hyper-rational senior manager at an automotive firm who views romance as nothing more than an inconvenient hormonal distraction. The series delves into the friction between professional ambitions and genuine emotional connection within the strict confines of standard working hours.
 5. The Blue Road
 The narrative balances grounded, procedural police work with tense psychological drama Launching on Netflix on November 20, this cross-border crime thriller unites Korean and Japanese talents for a dark investigation. Directed by Han Jun-hee, the story follows an unyielding investigative duo played by Son Suk-ku and Nagayama Eita as they unravel a long-buried cold case that reopens deep geopolitical tensions between neighboring nations. The narrative balances grounded, procedural police work with tense psychological drama, examining how unresolved crimes continue to cast long shadows over current diplomatic and human relationships.
 6. Crash (Season 2: Fury Road)
 Lee Min-ki, Kwak Sun-young, and Heo Sung-tae resume their roles for season 2 Arriving November 16 across ENA and Genie TV, the Traffic Crime Investigation (TCI) team returns for another high-octane season. Lee Min-ki, Kwak Sun-young, and Heo Sung-tae resume their roles as the quirky, specialized unit tackling bizarre vehicular offenses that traditional police divisions overlook. Combining kinetic car chases, technical crime-solving methods and sharp character comedy, this installment ramps up the stakes with dangerous highway syndicates and complex traffic-related mysteries.
 7. What a Boss Wants
 Sung Hoon stars as Kwon Do-hyeok, a perfectionist CEO suffering from severe insomnia and trauma Releasing November 11 on MBN and streaming internationally on Viki, this executive rom-com explores an unusual bond formed through music. Sung Hoon stars as Kwon Do-hyeok, a perfectionist CEO suffering from severe insomnia and trauma, who receives an unconventional medical recommendation to seek out a specific voice that calms his nervous system. His search leads him to an unconventional indie musician, played by Oh Se-young, whose chaotic, free-spirited approach to life completely disrupts his rigid routine.
 8. The Substitute
 The series follows an underground network of high-achieving proxy test-takers hired by elite families jisun park Premiering November 23 on TVING, this coming-of-age psychological thriller delves into the dark underbelly of academic pressure. Directed by Park So-yeon, the series follows an underground network of high-achieving proxy test-takers hired by elite families to fraudulently secure university admissions for privileged heirs. Bae Hyun-sung and Uhm Ji-won star in a tense narrative that examines the moral compromises, intense competition, and hidden corruption driving high-stakes academic society.
